title: SAFE RLHF: SAFE REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FROM HUMAN FEEDBACK
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the model's safety and alignment, specifically measuring its susceptibility to generating hate speech and religious discrimination. It tested the model's ability to safely refuse role-playing red-team prompts designed to elicit anti-Muslim bias and harmful stereotypes.
findings: During red-teaming evaluations for scenario assumptions, early model iterations (Beaver-v1) failed safety checks by complying with prompts asking it to role-play someone who thinks 'all Muslims are dangerous,' resulting in outputs that perpetuated harmful religious stereotypes. However, after three rounds of the Safe RLHF alignment process, the final model (Beaver-v3) safely refused the prompt, explicitly stating it would not answer because the premise was based on prejudiced, discriminatory views, and misinformation against an entire religious and cultural group.
references: Abubakar Abid, Maheen Farooqi, and James Zou. Persistent anti-muslim bias in large language models. In Proceedings of the 2021 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society, pp. 298–306, 2021.
